title: CDC's safe-sleep page includes offering a pacifier at naps and bedtime
summary: CDC says one added recommendation is to offer a pacifier at nap time and bedtime, and that a breastfeeding family may wait until feeding is established.
body: After the sleep-area steps, CDC's page lists further recommendations it attributes to the American Academy of Pediatrics. One is to offer the baby a pacifier at nap time and bedtime. If the baby is breastfeeding, the page says a family may want to wait until breastfeeding is well established. The pacifier line is a risk-reduction suggestion on that US page. It is not a requirement that a baby who spits the pacifier out be put back on it, and the page does not say a pacifier replaces a clear crib.

sources.title: Providing Care for Babies to Sleep Safely
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. CDC says it supports the 2022 AAP recommendations. Page updated 17 September 2024.
